scores.note: One line in NDPluginCircularBuff::processCallbacks, in the final 'Acquisition Completed' branch (finite preset trigger count reached): the other branch already did setIntegerParam(NDCircBuffSoftTrigger,0); this one did not, so the busy record $(P)$(R)Trigger (OUT=CIRC_BUFF_SOFT_TRIGGER, VAL=1) stayed at 'Trigger'/MINOR after a soft-triggered acquisition finished. Executed the shipped test: on the pin with the fix's new test case, test_SoftTriggerClearedAfterAcquisition fails (softTrigger 1 != 0); on pin+fix it passes, 4/4 cases. Real behavior change, but it only matters when a preset trigger count is used with soft trigger; operator can re-write 0 as workaround, so urgency is moderate. Applies with 1-line offset, builds clean, no API/ABI change. Only CircularBuff plugin is touched (leaf).

Only an asynPrint ERROR text in NDFileHDF5::writeFile adds the attribute name via destAtt->getName() (NDAttribute::getName returns name_.c_str(), never NULL, destAtt is non-null in this branch). Diagnostic aid only for a misconfigured dataset-destination attribute; no behavior change. Applies with offset 1, compiles without warnings. Not worth a patch by itself.

Adds #include <epicsTime.h> before <epicsMath.h> in NDPluginCircularBuff.cpp; upstream says it fixes a Windows compile error. Environment builds Linux only and the pin already compiles on Debian 13 gcc 14 with no change; epicsTime.h is a normal Base header present on every target. No runtime effect on any target. Zero value for this environment, risk-free to carry. Did not test GCC 15 (Ubuntu 26.04 not available here), so cannot exclude an unrelated benefit there, but nothing in the diff suggests one.

scores.note: Real diff: one line setIntegerParam(NDCircBuffSoftTrigger,0) in the final (acquisition completed) branch of NDPluginCircularBuff::processCallbacks, plus a Boost test. The other end-of-cycle branch (restart) and writeInt32 already zero it, so only the last iteration left the soft-trigger parameter at 1. Template NDCircularBuff.template defines $(P)$(R)Trigger as a busy record with OUT=CIRC_BUFF_SOFT_TRIGGER, so the stale 1 keeps the busy record busy (operators and put-callback/caput -c clients hang) after 'Acquisition Completed'. Executed: shipped test test_SoftTriggerClearedAfterAcquisition fails on the pin code with the test added (check softTrigger == 0 has failed [1 != 0]) and passes with the fix; the 3 existing CB tests pass in all builds. Clean -p1 apply, no ABI change, one-line leaf change in one plugin. Not security or memory-safety; no perf effect.

Real diff: one error asynPrint in NDFileHDF5::writeFile now also prints destAtt->getName(). destAtt is checked non-null in the enclosing if, getName() returns const char*, format has one added %s with one added argument, so no format mismatch and no new null deref. Only changes a trace-error message on a rare path (dataset destination attribute not a string); diagnostic value only. Applies with offset 1 line; builds clean (HDF5 enabled) and CB tests unaffected. No consumer behaviour change.

Real diff: adds #include <epicsTime.h> before <epicsMath.h> in NDPluginCircularBuff.cpp, a Windows-only compile-order workaround (commit message). On Linux NDPluginCircularBuff.h already pulls in epicsTime.h via NDPluginDriver.h (grep), so the include is redundant; pin compiles on gcc 14 without it. Zero functional, safety or ops effect for this Linux-only environment; nothing to fix, so urgency 0. Fit and locality maximal only because it is trivially safe.
